title: 1985 AHSME Problem 21
statement: How many integers \(x\) satisfy the equation \[ (x^2-x-1)^{x+2}=1? \]

solutions.text:
If the base is \(1,\) then \(x^2-x-1=1,\) giving \(x=-1\) and \(x=2.\) If the base is \(-1,\) then \(x(x-1)=0;\) only \(x=0\) makes the exponent \(x+2\) even. If the exponent is \(0,\) then \(x=-2,\) and its base is \(5,\) so it also works. Thus the four solutions are \(-2,\) \(-1,\) \(0,\) and \(2.\)

Therefore the correct answer is C.
hints: An integer power can equal \(1\) when the base is \(1,\) when the base is \(-1\) with even exponent, or when a nonzero base has exponent \(0\)
Solve those three cases separately and check every candidate
